title: 恒星的一生与它的行星家族
topic: The Life of a Star and Its Family of Planets

sentences.en: Today I want to walk you through one of the great stories in astronomy: the life of a star, and the family of worlds that can form around it.
sentences.zh: 今天我想带大家梳理天文学里最精彩的故事之一：一颗恒星的一生，以及可能围绕它形成的那一整个世界家族。

sentences.en: A star begins its life inside a nebula, a vast cloud of gas and dust drifting through interstellar space.
sentences.zh: 恒星的生命始于星云内部——那是一团在星际空间中飘荡的、由气体和尘埃组成的巨大云雾。

sentences.en: Under its own gravity, part of that cloud collapses, and as the material clumps together, a hot dense core begins to switch on and pour out light and radiation.
sentences.zh: 在自身引力作用下，云的一部分开始坍缩；随着物质聚拢，一个炽热致密的核心逐渐“点亮”，向外倾泻出光和辐射。

sentences.en: How bright a star truly is depends on its luminosity, the total energy it radiates each second, which is set by its size and its surface temperature.
sentences.zh: 一颗恒星究竟有多亮，取决于它的光度——也就是它每秒辐射出的总能量，而这由它的大小和表面温度共同决定。

sentences.en: Since we can't fly out and measure a star up close, astronomers rely on its spectrum, the band of colors we get when we spread its light out by wavelength, to read its temperature and chemical makeup.
sentences.zh: 既然我们无法飞过去近距离测量一颗恒星，天文学家便依靠它的光谱——把星光按波长展开后得到的那条彩色光带——来读出它的温度和化学成分。

sentences.en: Many stars are born together and stay bound by gravity in a cluster, and from Earth some of the brightest ones trace the familiar patterns we call a constellation.
sentences.zh: 许多恒星一同诞生，并靠引力束缚在一个星团中；从地球上看，其中一些最亮的恒星勾勒出我们熟悉的图案，也就是所谓的星座。

sentences.en: Our own Sun is an ordinary star, but the leftover disk of material around it slowly built the planets and countless smaller celestial bodies of the solar system.
sentences.zh: 我们的太阳只是一颗普通的恒星，但它周围残留的物质盘却缓慢地造就了太阳系里的行星和数不清的较小天体。

sentences.en: Each planet travels along its own orbit, and it also spins, or rotates, on its axis; Earth's rotation is what gives us day and night.
sentences.zh: 每颗行星都沿着自己的轨道运行，同时也绕着自转轴旋转，即自转；地球的自转正是昼夜交替的成因。

sentences.en: A rocky world like Mars is wrapped in a thin atmosphere, while an airless one like the Moon has none at all.
sentences.zh: 像火星这样的岩质天体裹着一层稀薄的大气层，而像月球这样没有空气的天体则完全没有大气。

sentences.en: The Moon is our nearest neighbor and Earth's only natural satellite, and its surface is scarred with craters left by ancient impacts.
sentences.zh: 月球是我们最近的邻居，也是地球唯一的天然卫星，它的表面布满了古老撞击留下的环形山。

sentences.en: Because the Moon has no atmosphere to burn things up, every meteorite that hits it can carve out a fresh crater that lasts for billions of years.
sentences.zh: 由于月球没有大气层来烧毁来物，每一块砸中它的陨石都能凿出一个崭新的、能保存数十亿年的环形山。

sentences.en: On Earth, most incoming space rocks never reach the ground; friction with the air makes them flare up as a meteor, a bright streak across the night sky.
sentences.zh: 在地球上，大多数闯入的太空岩石根本到不了地面；与空气的摩擦使它们燃起，化作流星，在夜空中划出一道亮痕。

sentences.en: Farther out lies a belt of asteroids, chunks of rock orbiting between Mars and Jupiter, along with icy comets that grow long glowing tails whenever they swing close to the Sun.
sentences.zh: 再往外是一条小行星带，那是在火星与木星之间运行的岩石碎块，还有一些冰质的彗星，每当它们掠近太阳时，就会拖出长长的发光尾巴。

sentences.en: To break free of a planet's gravity and reach these places, a spacecraft has to hit a very high velocity, its escape velocity.
sentences.zh: 要挣脱一颗行星的引力、抵达这些地方，航天器必须达到一个极高的速度，即它的逃逸速度。

sentences.en: And when the Sun, Moon, and Earth line up just right, one casts its shadow on another, producing a solar or a lunar eclipse.
sentences.zh: 而当太阳、月球和地球恰好排成一线时，其中一个便会把影子投到另一个上，从而形成日食或月食。

sentences.en: A massive star, however, dies hard: this stellar giant collapses and explodes as a supernova, briefly outshining an entire galaxy and flinging heavy elements back into space.
sentences.zh: 然而一颗大质量恒星死得惨烈：这颗恒星巨兽坍缩并爆发为超新星，一瞬间盖过整个星系的光芒，把重元素抛回太空。

sentences.en: Astronomers gather all this faint light with the telescope, and it reminds us that we are part of one grand, cosmic cycle of birth, death, and rebirth.
sentences.zh: 天文学家用望远镜收集这一切微弱的光，而这提醒着我们：我们本身就置身于一个宏大的、宇宙级的诞生、死亡与重生的循环之中。
